rows.stem: Kulhads (disposable cups made of clay) and disposable paper cups both are used as an alternative for disposable plastic cups. Which one of these two can be considered as a better alternative to plastic cups and why ?
rows.solution:
Disposable paper cups are the better alternative.

Kulhads are made from fertile top soil, so making them on a large scale would strip away the top soil that crops need. Paper cups are biodegradable: they decompose easily and do not pollute the environment.

rows.stem: Human beings are most adversely affected by the Biological Magnification. State the reason. Why can ordinary washing of the edibles (fruits and vegetables) not reduce the effect of biological magnification ?
rows.solution:
Human beings occupy the top level in most food chains. Harmful chemicals such as pesticides are not degraded and pass up the chain, getting more concentrated at each trophic level, so the maximum concentration accumulates in our bodies.

Ordinary washing cannot reduce the effect because the pesticides are not only on the surface. Plants absorb them from the soil along with water and minerals, so they are inside the fruits and vegetables and cannot be washed off.

rows.stem:
Draw the electron dot structure of the following :

(a) Cyclohexane

(b) Butane
rows.solution:
In an electron dot structure each shared pair is drawn between the two atoms, one electron of the pair as a dot and the other as a cross.

(a) Cyclohexane, \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}\): draw six carbon atoms joined in a ring. Between each pair of neighbouring carbon atoms draw one shared pair (a single bond), and on each carbon atom draw two hydrogen atoms, each sharing one pair with that carbon. Each carbon then has four shared pairs: two with carbon and two with hydrogen.

(b) Butane, \(\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}\): draw four carbon atoms in a straight chain, with one shared pair between each neighbouring pair of carbon atoms. The two end carbons each share pairs with three hydrogen atoms and the two middle carbons each with two, so every carbon has four shared pairs:

\(\mathrm{H_3C - CH_2 - CH_2 - CH_3}\), with every bond shown as a shared pair of electrons.

rows.stem: State the criteria used by Mendeleev for creating his Periodic Table. Compare the position of isotopes of elements in the Mendeleev’s Periodic Table and in the Modern Periodic Table.
rows.solution:
Mendeleev arranged the elements in order of increasing atomic mass, and placed elements with similar chemical properties in the same group, judging the similarity mainly by the formulae of their hydrides and oxides.

Isotopes have the same chemical properties but different atomic masses. Mendeleev's table, based on atomic mass, had no position for them: isotopes were discovered after his classification, and by his own criterion the isotopes of one element would need different places. In the Modern Periodic Table, which is based on atomic number, isotopes have the same atomic number, so all the isotopes of an element share the single position of that element and need no separate places.

rows.stem: An electric heater rated 1100 W operates at 220 V. Calculate (i) its resistance, and (ii) the current drawn by it.
Calculate the equivalent resistance of the following electric circuit :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit exists only in the drawing: a battery, a plug key and an ammeter (A) in a loop with a network of five resistors labelled 10 Ω, 10 Ω, 10 Ω, 20 Ω and 20 Ω. Which resistors are in series and which in parallel is withheld here because it is the answer. Page idx 4.
rows.solution:
In the circuit, a \(10\,\Omega\) resistor, a network in the middle and a \(20\,\Omega\) resistor are in series. In the network, two \(10\,\Omega\) resistors are in series with each other, and this pair is in parallel with a \(20\,\Omega\) resistor.

The series pair: \(R_s = 10 + 10 = 20\,\Omega\).

The pair in parallel with \(20\,\Omega\): \(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{20} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{10}\), so \(R_p = 10\,\Omega\).

Total equivalent resistance: \(R = 10 + 10 + 20 = 40\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Suggest any two contraceptive methods to control the size of human population and explain them.
rows.solution:
Any two:

1. Barrier method: a condom or diaphragm prevents the sperms from meeting the egg.

2. Chemical method (oral pills): the pills change the hormonal balance of the female body so that eggs are not released.

3. Copper-T or loop: a device placed in the uterus prevents pregnancy.

4. Surgical method: the vas deferens in the male is blocked, so sperms are not transferred, or the fallopian tube in the female is blocked, so the egg cannot reach the uterus. Fertilisation is prevented.

rows.stem: Mendel crossed two pea plants with visible contrasting characteristics and found that there were no half-way characteristics in the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) progeny. Explain the reason for this observation of Mendel.
rows.solution: The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants carry the factors for both contrasting traits, one from each parent, but only one of the two traits is expressed. The trait that is expressed is the dominant trait; the one that is not expressed in its presence is the recessive trait. So the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants show the dominant trait fully (for example, all tall when tall and short plants are crossed), and no half-way characteristics appear.

rows.stem: Justify the statement “Sex of the children will be determined by what they inherit from their father”.
rows.solution:
A mother has two X chromosomes (XX) and a father has one X and one Y chromosome (XY).

Every egg from the mother carries an X chromosome, so all children inherit an X from their mother. Half the sperms carry an X and half carry a Y. A child who inherits an X chromosome from the father (XX) is a girl, and a child who inherits a Y chromosome from the father (XY) is a boy. So the sex of the child depends on which chromosome it inherits from the father.

rows.stem:
Name the part/organ of the human female reproductive system

(a) where contraceptive devices such as loop or copper-T are placed to prevent pregnancy.

(b) which is blocked to prevent the transfer of eggs.

(c) where formation of green cells as ova takes place.

(d) from where the embryo gets nutrition from the mother’s blood.
rows.solution:
(a) Uterus.

(b) Fallopian tube (oviduct).

(c) Ovary. The paper prints "green cells as ova", a misprint for germ cells; because of it, CBSE awarded this half mark to every student.

(d) Placenta.

rows.stem: What are human-made ecosystems ? Give an example. Can a human-made ecosystem become a self-sustaining ecosystem ? Give reason to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
Human-made ecosystems are artificial ecosystems developed and maintained by human beings. Example: an aquarium (crop fields, gardens and parks are others).

No, a human-made ecosystem cannot become self-sustaining. It depends on human inputs: an aquarium has to be cleaned regularly, and fish food and fresh water have to be added, because it does not have enough producers and decomposers (bacteria) to replenish nutrients and break down wastes naturally.

rows.stem:
State the reason why

(i) carbon compounds have low melting and boiling points.

(ii) carbon compounds do not conduct electricity.

(iii) carbon can form only covalent compounds.
rows.solution:
(i) The forces of attraction between the molecules of carbon compounds are weak, so little energy is needed to separate them.

(ii) The bonding in carbon compounds is covalent and does not give rise to any ions (charged particles), so there is nothing to carry the current.

(iii) Carbon has four valence electrons. It cannot gain four electrons, because six protons cannot hold ten electrons, and it cannot lose four electrons, because that needs a large amount of energy. So it can only share electrons with other atoms, forming covalent compounds.

rows.stem:
What is a homologous series ? Find the difference in molecular mass between the two consecutive members of a homologous series. State how in a homologous series of carbon compounds the following properties vary with increase in molecular mass :

(i) Melting and boiling points

(ii) Chemical properties
rows.solution:
A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds that have the same functional group and similar chemical properties, in which each successive member differs from the previous one by a \(\mathrm{-CH_2-}\) unit.

Difference in molecular mass between consecutive members \(= \mathrm{CH_2} = 12 + 2 \times 1 = 14\) u.

(i) Melting and boiling points increase with increase in molecular mass.

(ii) Chemical properties remain similar, because they are decided by the functional group, which is the same for all members.

rows.subtopic: Early Attempts at the Classification of Elements
rows.stem:
In the following table, some elements have been arranged in a certain pattern :

| sa (do) | re (re) | ga (mi) | ma (fa) | pa (so) | da (la) | ni (ti) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H | Li | Be | B | C | N | O |
| F | Na | Mg | Al | Si | P | S |
| Cl | K | Ca | Cr | Ti | Mn | Fe |
| Co and Ni | Cu | Zn | Y | In | As | Se |
| Br | Rb | Sr | Ce and La | Zr | – | – |

Identify the periodic law with which the given table is associated. List two important features and two anomalies of the above periodic law.
rows.solution:
The table follows Newlands' Law of Octaves: the elements are arranged like the notes of the Indian musical scale (sa, re, ga, ma, pa, da, ni).

Important features:

1. The elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic mass.

2. Every eighth element had properties similar to the first, like the eighth note of a musical scale (for example, Na is the eighth element from Li).

Anomalies (any two):

1. The law worked well only for the lighter elements, up to calcium.

2. Newlands assumed that only 56 elements existed in nature and that no more would be discovered.

3. To fit elements into the table, two elements were put in one slot (Co and Ni), and unlike elements were placed together: Co and Ni with the halogens F, Cl and Br, and the metal Fe with the non-metals O and S.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: What is a Solenoid ? Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines around a current carrying solenoid. Mark on the pattern the region where the magnetic field is uniform.
rows.solution:
A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

Diagram: draw the solenoid as a long coil connected to a battery and a plug key. Inside the solenoid draw the field lines as straight, parallel, equally spaced lines running along its axis. Outside, the lines come out of one end, curve round the solenoid and enter the other end, like the field of a bar magnet, so one end behaves as a north pole and the other as a south pole. Put arrows on the lines: inside they run from the south end to the north end.

Mark the region inside the solenoid, where the lines are parallel and straight, as the region of uniform magnetic field.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
In the diagram given below, Coil – 1 is connected in series with a battery and a plug key while Coil – 2 is connected with a galvanometer.

(i) Why does the galvanometer show deflection only when the key (K) is plugged in and not when a steady current starts flowing in the circuit ?

(ii) What is observed in the galvanometer, when the key is plugged out ?

(iii) State the conclusion based on the observation of this activity.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - two coils, labelled Coil – 1 and Coil – 2, wound on one long cylindrical tube; Coil – 1 is wired to a battery and a plug key K, Coil – 2 to a galvanometer G. The stem states the connections, so the row is answerable from text. Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
(i) When the key is plugged in, the current in Coil-1 rises from zero, so the magnetic field around Coil-1, which also passes through Coil-2, changes. This change induces a current in Coil-2 and the galvanometer deflects. Once a steady current flows, the magnetic field stays constant, there is no change for Coil-2, no current is induced and the galvanometer returns to zero.

(ii) When the key is plugged out, the galvanometer again deflects momentarily, but in the opposite direction.

(iii) A current is induced in a coil only when the magnetic field linked with it changes. Here that happens only at the moment the key is plugged in or plugged out. This is electromagnetic induction.

rows.stem:
In the figure given below, a simple electric motor is shown :

As shown in the figure, the current in the coil ABCD flows from A to B in the arm AB and C to D in the arm CD.

(i) State the directions in which the arms AB and CD will experience a force.

(ii) Identify the part of the electric motor that reverses the flow of current in the coil ABCD and write its name.

(iii) After the reversal of flow of current in the coil ABCD, state the directions in which the arms AB and CD will experience a force.

(iv) Name the rule which is applied to determine the direction of force on a current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the drawing of the motor: two magnet blocks labelled N and S, a rectangular coil with corners labelled A, B, C and D carrying arrows, parts labelled P and Q and X and Y at the axle, and a battery with a plug key K. Parts (i) and (iii) need the placement of the poles relative to the coil, and (ii) needs the parts at the axle; both are withheld here because they decide the answers. Page idx 10.
rows.solution:
The magnetic field runs from the N pole to the S pole, across the coil.

(i) By Fleming's left-hand rule, arm AB experiences a force downward and arm CD a force upward. The two forces are opposite, so the coil rotates.

(ii) P and Q, the two halves of the split ring, form the commutator, which reverses the current in the coil every half rotation. (X and Y are the brushes that press against it.)

(iii) After the reversal the forces reverse: arm AB experiences a force upward and arm CD a force downward. So the coil keeps rotating in the same direction.

(iv) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points along the magnetic field and the middle finger along the current, the thumb points along the force on the conductor.

rows.stem: How do Mendel’s experiments show that the traits are inherited independently ? Explain.
rows.solution:
Mendel crossed pea plants differing in two pairs of contrasting traits: a plant with round, yellow seeds and a plant with wrinkled, green seeds.

All the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants had round, yellow seeds, so round and yellow are the dominant traits.

When the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants were self-pollinated, the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) progeny had four kinds of seeds in the ratio

round yellow : round green : wrinkled yellow : wrinkled green \(= 9 : 3 : 3 : 1\).

Besides the parental types (round yellow and wrinkled green), new combinations appeared: round green and wrinkled yellow, which were present neither in the parents nor in the \(\mathrm{F_1}\). If seed shape and seed colour were inherited together, only the parental combinations would appear. The new combinations show that the two traits are inherited independently of each other.

rows.stem: Find the equivalent resistance of arm A.
rows.context: Study the following electric circuit in which the resistors are arranged in three arms A, B and C :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the circuit exists only in the drawing: a 6 V battery, an ammeter and a plug key in a loop with arm A, followed by arms B and C between two junctions, each arm a row of three resistors. The resistor values are printed only in the drawing and are not restated here. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
Arm A has \(5\,\Omega\), \(15\,\Omega\) and \(20\,\Omega\) in series:

\(R_A = 5 + 15 + 20 = 40\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Calculate the equivalent resistance of the parallel combination of the arms B and C.
rows.context: Study the following electric circuit in which the resistors are arranged in three arms A, B and C :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the same drawing as Q14 (a): the shared passage says to study the circuit, so every part of the case study carries it. Page idx 12.

rows.stem: Determine the current that flows through the ammeter.
rows.context: Study the following electric circuit in which the resistors are arranged in three arms A, B and C :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the same drawing as Q14 (a): the shared passage says to study the circuit, so every part of the case study carries it. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
Arm A is in series with the parallel combination of B and C:

\(R = R_A + R_p = 40 + 20 = 60\,\Omega\).

\(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6}{60} = \dfrac{1}{10} = 0.1\) A.

rows.stem: Determine the current that flows in the ammeter when the arm B is withdrawn from the circuit.
rows.context: Study the following electric circuit in which the resistors are arranged in three arms A, B and C :
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the same drawing as Q14 (a): the shared passage says to study the circuit, so every part of the case study carries it. Page idx 12.
rows.solution:
With arm B withdrawn, arm A is in series with arm C alone:

\(R = 40 + 60 = 100\,\Omega\).

\(I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{6}{100} = 0.06\) A.

rows.stem: State the name of the organism in which binary fission takes place in a definite orientation. Also name the disease caused by this organism.
rows.context: The modes by which various organisms reproduce depend on the body design of the organisms. In asexual reproduction, a single individual parent produces offsprings without the involvement of gametes. This method is a common means of increasing the offsprings rapidly under favourable conditions. Asexual reproduction occurs mostly in unicellular organisms, some plants and certain simple multicellular animals.
rows.solution: *Leishmania* divides by binary fission in a definite orientation. It causes kala-azar.

rows.stem: List any two advantages of producing plants through vegetative propagation.
rows.context: The modes by which various organisms reproduce depend on the body design of the organisms. In asexual reproduction, a single individual parent produces offsprings without the involvement of gametes. This method is a common means of increasing the offsprings rapidly under favourable conditions. Asexual reproduction occurs mostly in unicellular organisms, some plants and certain simple multicellular animals.
rows.solution:
Any two:

1. Plants can bear flowers and fruits much earlier than plants produced from seeds.

2. The new plants are genetically similar to the parent plant, so its desirable characters are kept.

3. Plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds, such as banana, orange, rose and jasmine, can be propagated.

rows.stem: Explain the process of budding in Hydra.
rows.context: The modes by which various organisms reproduce depend on the body design of the organisms. In asexual reproduction, a single individual parent produces offsprings without the involvement of gametes. This method is a common means of increasing the offsprings rapidly under favourable conditions. Asexual reproduction occurs mostly in unicellular organisms, some plants and certain simple multicellular animals.
rows.solution: In *Hydra*, a bud develops as an outgrowth because of repeated cell division at one specific site on the body. The bud grows into a tiny individual with its own tentacles, and when fully mature it detaches from the parent body and becomes a new independent individual.

rows.stem:
What happens when

(I) a spirogyra filament matures and attains a considerable length, and

(II) a sporangia in Rhizopus bursts on maturation ?
rows.context: The modes by which various organisms reproduce depend on the body design of the organisms. In asexual reproduction, a single individual parent produces offsprings without the involvement of gametes. This method is a common means of increasing the offsprings rapidly under favourable conditions. Asexual reproduction occurs mostly in unicellular organisms, some plants and certain simple multicellular animals.
rows.solution:
(I) The mature *Spirogyra* filament simply breaks up into smaller pieces (fragmentation), and each fragment grows into a new individual.

(II) The sporangium releases its spores. The spores, carried by air, germinate on a moist surface and develop into new *Rhizopus* individuals.
